- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing downward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model delays mean reversion, especially when sentiment shifts from negative to neutral/positive — prices often overshoot before settling.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes: model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, leading to overprediction in the following days.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes trend continuation longer than actual — prices often revert to prior 10-15 day average after strong moves.
- Sentiment-driven horizon mismatch: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment swings, not aligning with longer-term price behavior.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3-day horizon — sentiment decay often underestimates price correction speed.
